title: Genome editing in the choanoflagellate Salpingoeca rosetta
author: David Booth
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bx58pq9w
materials: Seed a large culture of S. rosetta .
Deliver gene editing cargo via nucleofection.

steps.title: Prepare S. rosetta culture
steps.instruction: Two days before transfection inoculate 120 mL high‑nutrient media (Falcon 525 cm² rectangular straight‑neck 3‑layer flask, Corning #353143) with a Salpingoeca rosetta culture feeding on E. pacifica (SrEpac, ATCC #PRA‑390) to a final density of 8 000 cells · mL⁻¹; grow for 48 h at 22 °C, 60 % humidity.

steps.title: Resuspend crRNA and tracrRNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend crRNA (IDT custom order, duplex buffer IDT #11‑01‑03‑01, 30 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.5, 100 mM potassium acetate) to 200 µM; resuspend tracrRNA (IDT #1072534, same duplex buffer) to 200 µM.

steps.title: Anneal crRNA and tracrRNA to gRNA
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of the 200 µM crRNA and 200 µM tracrRNA to obtain 100 µM gRNA; incubate at 95 °C for 5 min in an aluminum block, then allow to cool at room temperature to 25 °C; store gRNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare repair oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Dissolve each repair oligo (IDT custom order) to 250 µM in 10 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.5; incubate at 55 °C for 1 h; store at –20 °C. Before nucleofection, reconfirm full dissolution by a 55 °C, 1 h incubation.

steps.title: Assemble SpCas9 ribonucleoprotein
steps.instruction: In a 0.2 mL PCR tube place 2 µL of 20 µM EnGen SpCas9 NLS (NEB #M0646T); add 2 µL of 100 µM gRNA (step 3) and gently pipette up/down to mix; incubate the 4 µL RNP at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Prepare SF Nucleofection Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine buffer B (smaller volume, also called supplement 1) with buffer A (larger volume) from the Lonza SF Cell Line 96‑well Nucleofector Kit (V4SC‑2096); keep on ice; the combined buffer can be stored at 4 °C for up to 3 months. Aliquot 900 µL of buffer A and 200 µL of buffer B to avoid spoilage.

steps.title: Prepare priming buffer
steps.instruction: a) Dilute papain stock (1 mM, Sigma #P3125‑100MG) to 100 µM in dilution buffer (50 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.5, 200 mM NaCl, 20 % v/v glycerol, 10 mM cysteine); sterile‑filter (0.22 µm) and keep on ice; b) Prepare the remaining components (40 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.5, 34 mM lithium citrate, 50 mM L‑cysteine, 15 % w/v PEG 8000); sterile‑filter and store at –80 °C; do not mix papain with this solution until just before use; warm the priming buffer to room temperature before adding to cells.

steps.title: Wash and count S. rosetta cells
steps.instruction: Homogenize the 120 mL culture by vigorous shaking, split into three 40 mL aliquots in 50 mL conical tubes; shake each aliquot and centrifuge 5 min at 2000 × g, 22 °C; remove supernatant leaving ~2 mL cloudy fraction, then gently remove remaining liquid near the pellet; resuspend pellets in 50 mL artificial seawater, combine into one tube and shake; repeat centrifugation (5 min, 2000 × g, 22 °C), supernatant removal, resuspension in 50 mL seawater; centrifuge a third time (5 min, 2200 × g, 22 °C), remove supernatant; finally resuspend the pellet in 400 µL artificial seawater ("washed cells"). Prepare 100 µL aliquots of 5 × 10⁷ cells · mL⁻¹. For counting, dilute 2 µL washed cells into 196 µL seawater, add 2 µL 37.5 % formaldehyde, vortex, and count on a hemacytometer or Luna‑FL (Logos Biosystems L20001); note this dilution is 1:100. After counting, dilute washed cells to 5 × 10⁷ cells · mL⁻¹ and aliquot 100 µL (one aliquot supplies 12 nucleofections).

steps.title: Prime cells for nucleofection
steps.instruction: Spin each 100 µL cell aliquot at 800 × g, 22 °C for 5 min; remove supernatant with a gel‑loading tip; combine priming buffer components (step 6) to make final priming buffer (40 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.5, 34 mM lithium citrate, 50 mM L‑cysteine, 15 % w/v PEG 8000, 1 µM papain); resuspend each cell pellet in 100 µL priming buffer; incubate 35 min at room temperature; add 10 µL of 50 mg mL⁻¹ BSA to quench proteolysis; centrifuge 5 min at 1250 × g, 22 °C; remove supernatant; resuspend each pellet in 25 µL SF Buffer (step 5) to obtain "primed cells"; keep primed cells on ice.

steps.title: Combine RNP, repair template, and primed cells
steps.instruction: To the 4 µL SpCas9 RNP (step 4) add 16 µL ice‑cold SF Buffer (step 5); if using multiple gRNAs, combine the separate RNPs first then add buffer; add 2 µL repair oligo (step 4) and 2 µL primed cells (step 8); total volume = 24 µL (the "nucleofection mix").

steps.title: Perform nucleofection and recovery
steps.instruction: Transfer the 24 µL nucleofection mix into one well of a 96‑well nucleofection plate; set a pipette to 100 µL and have recovery buffer (10 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.5, 0.9 M sorbitol, 8 % w/v PEG 8000) ready; pulse the plate with program CM156 on a 4D‑Nucleofector Core Unit (Lonza AAF‑1002B) using the 96‑well Shuttle Device (Lonza AAM‑1001S); immediately add 100 µL ice‑cold recovery buffer to the well and tap gently to mix; let cells rest 5 min; gently pipette up/down, then transfer the entire 124 µL (mix + recovery) into 2 mL low‑nutrient media in one well of a 6‑well plate; incubate 30 min at 22 °C, 60 % humidity.

steps.title: Post‑nucleofection culture and selection
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of 10 mg mL⁻¹ E. pacifica (prepared by resuspending a frozen 10 mg pellet in 1 mL artificial seawater) to each 6‑well; incubate 24 h at 22 °C, 60 % humidity; thereafter add 10 µL of 1 µg mL⁻¹ cycloheximide to the 2 mL culture, handle with care; incubate 96 h in cycloheximide before genotyping and clonal isolation.
